मान्यवर, आरबीआई द्वारा जारी ताजा आंकड़ों के अनुसार जब से भारतीय जनता पार्टी की सरकार देश में आई है, तब से अब तक बैंकों में ग्रॉस एनपीए में लगभग 4 गुना बढ़ोतरी हुई है । 

यह एन.पी.ए. क्या है? महोदय, यह एन.पी.ए. कर्ज की वह रकम है, जो बैंकों से ले ली जाती है और वापस नहीं की जाती है । भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक कहता है कि बैंकों का ग्रॉस एन.पी.ए. जो 31 मार्च, 2014 को 2.13 लाख करोड़ रुपये था, वह मार्च, 2018 में बढ़ कर 10.39 लाख करोड़ रुपये हो गया है । आर.बी.आई. द्वारा जारी आंकड़ों में अगर सरकारी बैंकों के एन.पी.ए. पर नजर डाली जाए तो उसकी स्थिति और भी बदतर है । वर्ष 2014 में 2.27 लाख करोड़ रुपये था, जो वर्ष 2018 में बढ़ कर 8.95 लाख करोड़ रुपये हो गया है ।

मान्यवर, मैं आपसे इतना ही कहना चाहता हूं कि यह सरकार बहुत अच्छे तरीके से सपने दिखाती है । सपने बेचना और सपनों की मार्केटिंग करना अगर कोई सीखे तो इनसे सीखे । जब ये पहली बार आए थे तो कहा था कि काला धन वापस लेकर आएंगे, पन्द्रह-पन्द्रह लाख रुपये सबके खाते में आएंगे । अब कह रहे हैं कि अगले चार सालों में किसानों की आमदनी दोगुना कर देंगे । पता नहीं कौन-सी रफ्तार से, कौन-सी जादू की छड़ी से ये ऐसा करने वाले हैं? ये कह रहे हैं कि हमारी इकोनॉमी 5 ट्रिलियन डॉलर की होगी । हम चाहते हैं कि यह हो, देश का हर व्यक्ति चाहता है कि यह हो, लेकिन इनकी जो नीयत है, वह साफ नहीं है । सपने दिखाना ये बहुत अच्छे तरीके से जानते हैं ।

इंश्योरेंस सेक्टर को जिस तरीके से बेलगाम छोड़ा गया है, ‘प्रधान मंत्री फसल बीमा योजना’ के तहत जो इंश्योरेंस होता है तो यहां पर कई साथी किसान परिवार से आते हैं, वे अपने दिल पर हाथ रखकर बता दें कि किस किसान को उस बीमा के तहत मुआवजा मिलता है । किसानों के मरते में दो लात और मारने का काम होता है । इंश्योरेंस के नाम पर किसानों से प्रीमियम वसूल किया जाता है । एक तो वह कर्ज पर ब्याज देता है और ऊपर से उससे और प्रीमियम वसूल किया जाता है । यह ‘प्रधान मंत्री फसल बीमा योजना’ सिर्फ कॉर्पोरेट हाउसेज को इंश्योरेंस के माध्यम से फायदा पहुँचाने के लिए लाई गई है ।

मान्यवर, आप सब जानते हैं कि पिछले 45 सालों में बेरोजगारी सबसे ज्यादा बढ़ी है । यह मैं नहीं कह रहा हूं, बल्कि ये आँकड़े कह रहे हैं । लेकिन, उससे लड़ने के लिए कुछ नहीं हुआ । अभी तो सरकार लेबर लॉज़ में भी भारी परिवर्तन करने के संकेत दे रही है । यह भी एक जनविरोधी निर्णय है । उद्योगपतियों को ‘हायर एण्ड फायर’ करने का अधिकार यह सरकार देने वाली है । इसी के माध्यम से कर्मचारियों की छँटनी होने वाली है । 

महोदय, मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि ऐसा पहली बार हुआ है कि सरकार के जो उपक्रम मुनाफे में चल रहे हैं, उनके भी शेयर्स बेचने की बात यह सरकार कर रही है । इससे पहले कभी किसी सरकार ने, चाहे वह काँग्रेस की सरकार रही हो, चाहे संयुक्त मोर्चा की सरकार रही हो या एन.डी.ए. की वाजपेयी जी की सरकार रही हो, कभी भी मुनाफे में चल रहे पब्लिक सेक्टर अंडरटेकिंग्स के शेयर्स को बेचने की बात नहीं हुई । पहली बार इस सरकार ने यह संकेत दिए हैं कि वे मुनाफे में चल रहे पी.एस.यूज़. के शेयर्स बेचेगी । ऐसा क्यों है? इसका सीधा मकसद है कि जो कुछ बची-खुची सरकारी नौकरियां हैं, जो दलितों को और पिछड़े वर्गों के नौजवानों को मिलती हैं, उनके हाथों से वह रोजगार छीनना है, वे सरकारी नौकरियां, उन दलितों और पिछड़ों से छीननी हैं । इसलिए ये मुनाफे में चल रहे सरकारी उपक्रमों को बेचने की सोच रहे हैं ।

महोदय, इस सरकार ने कॉर्पोरेट टैक्स में भारी कमी की, बैंकों के कर्ज़ माफ किए । यह सरकार बड़े पूंजीपतियों को बेतहाशा फायदा पहुंचा रही है । वहीं दूसरी ओर, देश की गरीब जनता को महँगाई के बोझ के नीचे दबाने का काम यह सरकार कर रही है । 

इस बजट में डीजल तथा पेट्रोल की कीमत को बढ़ाया गया है । इससे आम आदमी के इस्तेमाल में आने वाली हर जरूरी चीज़ों की कीमत में वृद्धि होगी । सरकार के इस फैसले से देश की गरीब जनता की परेशानी और बढ़ेगी । गरीब आदमी को राहत देना तो दूर, सरकार के इस बजट ने गरीबों की मेहनत की कमाई छीनकर अपने जेब में डालने का काम किया है । यह कैसी सरकार है, जो गरीबों से छीनकर अमीरों में बाँटने का काम कर रही है । …(व्यवधान)

सभापति महोदय, मैं इतना ही कहना चाहता हूं …(व्यवधान) निशिकांत दुबे जी को तो इनकी पार्टी ने इसीलिए रखा है, अभी तक इन्होंने रूल बुक नहीं निकाली है ।…(व्यवधान) वह रूल बुक निकाल सकते थे ।…(व्यवधान) इनमें सच्चाई सुनने की क्षमता नहीं है । वे सच्चाई नहीं सुनना चाहते हैं । जब इस संसद के अंदर गरीब आदमी की बात होगी, शोषित वर्ग की बात होगी, किसान की बात होगी, तो वे नहीं सुनेंगे । इनके जो मास्टर्स हैं, जिनके द्वारा चुनावों में हज़ारों-करोड़ों रुपये आता है, इन्हें तो उनकी बात यहां करनी है । जब हम गरीब तथा किसान की बात करते हैं, तो वे डिस्टर्ब करते हैं।…(व्यवधान)

सभापति महोदय, मैं आपके माध्यम से कहना चाहता हूं कि यह बजट गरीब विरोधी है, किसान विरोधी है, नौज़वान और महिला विरोधी है । मैं अभी भी आपके माध्यम से वित्त मंत्री जी से कहना चाहूंगा कि बजट को पास कराने से पहले सोचिए कि इस देश में जो गरीब हैं, जो वंचित हैं, जो शोषित हैं, उनके बारे में आपको कुछ करना होगा ।…(व्यवधान) यह बात अलग है कि आप ईवीएम के माध्यम से यहां आए हैं, लेकिन फिर भी आए हैं, तो आप कम से कम गरीब और शोषितों के बारे में कुछ सोचिए। 

महोदय, मैं इन्हीं बातों के साथ आपको एक बार फिर से धन्यवाद देता हूं । बहुत-बहुत 

शुक्रिया ।

श्री अधीर रंजन चौधरी (बहरामपुर): सभापति महोदय, मैं आपसे एक बात कहना चाहता हूं कि अभी बजट पर चर्चा चल रही है, लेकिन हमारे वित्त मंत्री यहां से नदारद हैं ।…(व्यवधान)

SHRI SUNIL DATTATRAY TATKARE (RAIGAD): Sir, thank you very much for giving me the opportunity to speak on the General Budget. I also thank Supriya ji. 

Sir, this is my maiden speech in the 17th Lok Sabha. So, I dedicate my maiden speech to the country’s visionary leader, hon. Shri Sharad Pawar, who has been working for India for six decades and who has been unbeaten in 15 elections. He laid the foundation of second agricultural revolution in the country. I also mention the name of one more leader of the country, the architect of Tamil Nadu, Shri M. Karunanidhi, who was also unbeaten in thirteen elections. So, Salaam Pawar Sahab and Vanakam Karunanidhi ji. 

Sir, I would like to mention that I come from a small town, Roha, the same town that late Shri C. D. Deshmukh also belonged to. He was appointed the first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in 1943. He was the first Finance Minister from 1952-56. He was the pioneer of LIC. He resigned for the formation of the Sanyukt Maharashtra Movement. I am from that area.

Some of my colleagues from Gujarat must be knowing about Shri Pandurang Shastri Athawale, the great philosopher of Shrimad Bhagwad Geeta, Swadhyaya Pariwar. He was also from Roha. 

I pay my respect to these honourable personalities.

Sir, the Government created history by getting a huge mandate from the people of India the second time. In 1985, when late Shri Rajiv Gandhi headed the Congress Party, they had such a majority. After a long span, people have given you the majority but you have failed to live up to the expectations of the farmers, the middle class and the youth.

The Government is using fancy words but allocations to various sectors present a grim picture with regard to its commitment ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas and Sabka Vishwas’. There is a severe economic crisis in the country today which the Government fails to acknowledge. The Government is talking about doubling the income of the farmers. When my mentor Shri Pawar Ji was the Agriculture Minister, Swaminathan Committee was appointed. That Committee had given its recommendations. But there is not a single word regarding the acceptance of Swaminathan Committee recommendations in this Budget presented by hon. Finance Minister.

There is no procurement and there is no increase in minimum support price. I know this because I come from a rice-procurement area. In 2004 during Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ji’s Government, Rs.450 was given per quintal. When my mentor was the Agriculture Minister, it was Rs.1,550. But in the last five years, there has been no increase in this minimum support price. Even for procurement of food grains, no special provision has been made. It is unfortunate. 

Further, Aadhaar is now linked to the IT. About 70 per cent of the country’s economy is in the agriculture sector. By connecting it to Aadhaar, is the Government going to impose income tax on the poor farmers of India? The Government will have to answer this question definitely. 

Instead of providing relief to the common man and the middle-class families by giving tax relief, the Government has hiked the Excise Duty on petrol and diesel which will be a burden on the common man who has been bearing the brunt of excise taxation on petrol and diesel. It is my demand that petrol and diesel be brought under GST to lower their prices and benefit the consumer. 

The Government always talks about Startup India. In a survey conducted in 2018 on 33,000 startups, 80 per cent said that they received no benefit from the Startup India scheme and over 50 per cent said that corruption remains to be the single biggest challenge to business apart from bureaucratic inefficiency. 

The share of loans given to entrepreneurs belonging to SC and ST communities under the scheme has so far been negligible. Thus far, only six per cent bank loans have been given to Dalits or Adivasis and less than 20 per cent is given to women. As a result of Excise Duty hike, inflation may take place. 

The Government has launched its Ayushman Bharat scheme. When I was the Finance Minister in my State, our State Government had implemented a scheme called Rajiv Gandhi Jeevandayee Yojana. An amount of Rs.4,000 crore was given in the Interim Budget presented in February, 2019. However, it is expected to benefit mostly the private hospitals and not the beneficiaries. So, to implement this scheme, you will have to take the healthcare further. 

Under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, as on May 2018, only 45 per cent of the claims made have been settled for farmers as per the Annual Report of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India. An amount of Rs.11,900 crore was collected by 11 private sector insurance companies whereas they paid claims worth Rs.8,000 crore only. Especially in Maharashtra, my colleague from Shiv Sena, who are allies of the NDA Government, has also quoted these things. 

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana saw 4.5 per cent reduction in allocation. In his 2018 Budget Speech, Finance Minister Arun Jaitley Ji committed to constructing 1,000 crore houses by the end of 2019. Only 63 lakh houses or 61 per cent of the target has been achieved by December, 2018.

In the reply given in Lok Sabha on 25th June, 2019, the Ministry of Rural Development stated that they had completed the construction of just above 81 lakh houses against the sanctioned number of over 99 lakh houses.

Maharashtra is a pioneer in local governance. The expenditure by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj dropped from Rs. 3,390 crore in 2014-15 to Rs. 871 crore, a decline of 74 per cent. This Government looks very keen on turning a blind eye towards strengthening Panchayati Raj and local governance.

Sir, I would like to mention about the reduction in total spending on education. Despite the claims of the present Government to improve education across the country, the total expenditure has not seen an increase in proportion to the Budget. It has actually fallen from what it was in 2017-18. I would like to give an example. The spending in 2017-18 was 3.7 per cent; spending in 2018-19 was 3.4 per cent; and the spending in 2019-20 is going to be around 3.4 per cent. I would like to say here that you are going to set up international universities in the country and foreign students will be allowed in those universities. Sir, through you, I would like to ask the hon. Minister as to what will happen to the reservation? When foreign students are allowed in those universities, what will happen to the SC/ST, OBC reservation? That will be the problem therein.

I would like to ask the Minister regarding the PSUs, about which my colleague also mentioned here. The profit-making PSUs are also likely to be disinvested. You had given the assurance that two crore jobs will be created every year. An hon. Member stated earlier that even profit-making PSUs are going to be disinvested. If that is the case, what will happen to the youngsters who are waiting for the jobs?

Sir, I would like to ask about Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. Now the Budget for this is Rs. 80,000 crore. I would like to mention about my Raigad district here. Since the last three years, not a single rupee has been spent on this particular scheme.

Sir, I would like to point out that this country is a secular country. Coming to the reduction in funds for minorities, Sir, post-matric scholarship scheme is there for the minorities. The budget for this scheme was Rs. 692 crore in 2018-19 and Rs. 496 crore in 2019-20 it is. So, there is a decline of 28 per cent. For the National Minorities Development and the Finance Corporation, the budget was Rs. 165 crore in 2018-19 and Rs. 60 crore in 2019-20. So, there is a decline of 64 per cent. For Maulana Azad Education Foundation, the budget allocation was Rs. 125 crore in 2018-19, and it is Rs. 90 crore in 2019-20. So, there is a decline of Rs. 28 crore.

Sir, I would like to mention one thing here. In Bharat Mala project, there is one highway which goes from Mumbai to Goa, and then from Karnataka to Kerala. We have been reminding the Government about that stretch from Mumbai to Goa for the last 40 years. The hon. Minister, Shri Gadkari is an influential Minister in NDA. I would like to bring to the notice of the Treasury Benches that in Maharashtra he is not known by the name of Nitin Gadkari, but by the name of Nitin Roadkari. But I do not know whether he is helpless or what, this road is not being constructed. I would like to ask that what had happened to that road. Same is the case regarding Sagarmala Project also. So, it is pending.

Sir, I would like to bring to their notice through you, that the highest civilian award of Republic of India, Bharat Ratna has been awarded since last six decades.

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Please conclude now.

SHRI SUNIL DATTATRAY TATKARE: In 1958, Maharshi Dhondo Karve who was born in Dapoli in Ratnagiri district worked for the women’s welfare. Mahatma Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule were from Dapoli. Pandurang Vaman Kane who was awarded the Bharat Ratna award in 1963, for his scholarly work that spanned 40 years of active academic research, which resulted in 6,500 pages history of Dharmashastra.

Shri Vinoba Bhave was born in Gagode in my Raigad district and translated the Gita in Marathi language titled as Gitai. Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar was born in Mhow but his childhood was spent in Mandangad, Ambawade. These four Bharat Ratna awardees belong to only two talukas. So, the Ratnagiri district should be declared as a tourism district. Shri Nanasaheb Dharmadhikari, the recipient of ‘Maharashtra Bhushan’ which is the highest civilian award of Maharashtra, is also from my Raigad district. So, the circuit of tourism should be there. The new generation should be aware as to what sacrifice our people have made for this country. Lastly, I would like to say a few words in Marathi.

*Government of Maharashtra has sent a proposal to Government of India to accord a classical language status to Marathi language. Power and pride of Marathi language is quite evident in many books like Dyaneshwari, Sant Tukaram and Warkari literature, Mahanubhav Sect literature and in other forms of literature written by various Marathi saints. Saint Dyaneshwar Mauli had said that our Marathi language is greater and sweeter than the nectar. 

Hence, classical language status should be accorded to Marathi. You people only talk about nationalism. But, many Marathi poets like Sane Guruji, Kusumagraj have elaborated and celebrated the greatness of Marathi language in their poems. I would request Union Government to accord classical language status to Marathi immediately and also allow me to speak in Marathi for pressing this demand till it is fulfilled*.

HON. CHAIRPERSON: You can speak in English or Hindi, but Marathi translator is not here as you have not given prior notice. 

SHRI SUNIL DATTATRAY TATKARE: I will speak in English now so that the Minister can understand. Bank of India is the lead bank of my Raigad district. Rs. 11,000 crore have been deposited by the common people. Only for the NPA of Rs. 60 lakhs, the branch in a small village of Mhsala Taluka has been closed. The villagers are now required to go 22 kilometres away to the taluka place. 

Shrimati Supriya Sule had asked one question about CSR fund. Our Raigad district has a very high investment from the Government of India, the State Government and private entrepreneurs, but no CSR funds are allotted to my Raigad district. Even the CSR funds of RCF and JNPT have not been given to our district. So, I request that the CSR fund should be given to our district. 

श्री जगदम्बिका पाल (डुमरियागंज): माननीय सभापति जी, आपने मुझे माननीय वित्त मंत्री जी द्वारा प्रस्तुत किए गए जनरल बजट पर हो रही चर्चा में भाग लेने का मौका दिया, इसके लिए मैं आपका आभारी हूं । मैं आदरणीय वीरेन्द्र सिंह जी को भी धन्यवाद देता हूं ।

मैं आपके माध्यम से कहना चाहता हूं कि आज भी एक ऐसा भारत था जो ग्रामीण भारत है, जहां आज भी गांव में मकान नहीं था, शौचालय नहीं था, गांव में बिजली कनैक्शन नहीं था, गांव में क्लीन एनर्जी उज्ज्वला गैस का चूल्हा नहीं था । गांव में सौभाग्य योजना में कनैक्शन नहीं था । किसानों के पास खाद और पेस्टिसाइड के लिए पैसा नहीं था । एक तरफ दिल्ली, लखनऊ, अहमदाबाद या मुंबई का भारत था, जहां रात को भी दिन लगता था । जो विषमताएं और विषंगतियां थीं, पहली बार मोदी जी ने तय किया कि ग्रामीण भारत, जो अभाव का भारत है और जो शहरी भारत है, इन दोनों भारत के बीच के अंतर को हमारी सरकार समाप्त करके एक भारत का निर्माण करेगी । उस भारत के संकल्प के लिए इस बजट को प्रस्तुत किया गया है । उस दिशा में हम आगे बढ़े हैं । 

अगर आज देखें तो वर्ष 2019-20 में करोड़ों किसानों के लिए सरकार ने बजट दिया है । माननीय सदस्य जो आलोचना कर रहे हैं, उन्होंने शायद इसे पढ़ा न हो । आप देखिए कि वर्ष 2018-19 में जब कृषि बजट दिया था, वह आजादी के बाद पिछले वर्ष का सबसे हाइएस्ट बजट 57,600 करोड़ रुपये का था । इस चुनाव के पहले वर्ष 2018-19 में 57,600 करोड़ रुपये देश के किसानों को दिये गये थे । उस समय भी सदन में चर्चा हुई थी कि हम देश के कृषि और किसानों को आत्मनिर्भर बनाने और उनकी आय को दोगुना करने के लिए पिछली सरकारों की तुलना में हाइएस्ट बजट दे रहे हैं। आज एक साल बाद वर्ष 2019-20 के लिए हमने कृषि का परिव्यय 1,30,485 करोड़ रुपये का बजट एलोकेट किया है । मैं निश्चित रूप से देश के करोड़ों किसानों की तरफ से सरकार को बधाई देना चाहता हूं । पिछले बजट की तुलना में इस बार के बजट में किसानों के लिए 140 प्रतिशत की बढ़ोतरी की गई है । 

मैं एक बात और कहना चाहता हूं कि इस सरकार को कोई सफाई नहीं देनी है । पिछले पांच वर्षों में हमारी सरकार ने जो संकल्प लिया है, उस संकल्प को पूरा किया है । चाहे सरकार ने कहा हो कि निश्चित तौर पर हम देश के 18 हजार गांवों में, आजादी के बाद अगर बिजली नहीं थी तो इसके लिए कौन जिम्मेदार है, कौन-सी सरकारें जिम्मेदार थीं कि 18 हजार गांवों में, आजादी 1947 में मिली हो और वर्ष 2017-18 तक 18 हजार गांवों में बिजली न हो । इसी सदन में प्रधान मंत्री मोदी ने खड़े होकर कहा था कि चाहे नार्थ ईस्ट का कोई आखिरी गांव हो, जहां पोल नहीं पहुंच सकता हो या कन्याकुमारी से लेकर कश्मीर तक किसी भी राज्य का कोई गांव हो, किसी पार्टी की भी सरकार हो लेकिन एन.डी.ए. की सरकार हर गांव में, हर मजरे में विद्युतीकरण करने के लिए संकल्पित है । उन्होंने उन 18 हजार गांवों का विद्युतीकरण करके दिखाया । आज हम कह सकते हैं कि आजादी के बाद अगर देश के हर गांव इलेक्ट्रिफाइड हुए हैं, तो यह हमारी सरकार की देन है । आज फिर यह संकल्प दिया है कि इस देश के हर घर को हम मुफ्त बिजली का कनेक्शन देंगे, चाहे वह गरीबी रेखा के नीचे हो या गरीबी रेखा के ऊपर हो, सभी को मुफ्त कनेक्शन देंगे । आज एक-एक जनपद में, मेरी लोक सभा क्षेत्र में 300-400 करोड़ रुपये दिए जा रहे हैं । एक-एक घर का सर्वे हो रहा है, चाहे वह घर दूर खेत, खलिहान में हो, उसको भी हम बिजली का कनेक्शन मुफ्त में दे रहे हैं । कल्पना कीजिए कि कुछ सालों पहले कैसे बच्चों को किसी स्टेशन पर पढ़ना पड़ता था? इस गरीबी को, इस अभाव को वही समझ सकता है, जिन्होंने बचपन में खुद देखा था ।

एक साल में एनपीए एक लाख करोड़ रुपये कम हुए हैं, चार लाख करोड़ रुपये का रीयलाइजेशन हुआ है । मैं समझता हूं, ये आंकड़े हैं । चार लाख करोड़ रुपये की रिकवरी हुई है । इनसॉल्‍वेंसी एंड बैंक्रप्सी कोड बनने के बाद या सरफेसी एक्ट बनने के बाद 13.8 प्रतिशत लोन की वृद्धि हुई है । जो बैंक डूब रहे थे, तमाम बैंक दीवालिया हो रहे थे । बैंकों में गरीबों की पूंजी थी, जो बैंक में जमा कर रहे थे, लेकिन उनकी निकासी नहीं हो पा रही थी, क्योंकि बैंक दीवालिया हो रहे थे । आज उन बैंकों को बूस्ट करने के लिए पहली बार इस बजट में 70 हजार करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है । इसके लिए मैं देश के उन सभी जमाकर्ताओं की तरफ से उनको बधाई देना चाहता हूं । आज पांच लाख रुपये तक की आय वालों पर कोई टैक्स नहीं है । यह पहली बार हुआ है । पहले यह सीमा ढाई लाख रुपये की थी । वित्त मंत्री जी और हम लोग लगातार तीन बार इस सदन में रहे हैं । हम ने हमेशा देखा है कि कर की सीमा 25 हजार या 50 हजार रुपये बढ़ाई जाती थी । जब अंतरिम बजट आया तभी यह तय हुआ कि पांच लाख की आय पर कोई कर नहीं लगेगा । अगर आप सैस और टैक्स के बारे में कहते हैं तो निश्चित तौर पर देश की बुनियादी ढांचों और देश की आवश्यकताओं की पूर्ति करने के लिए हम जवाबदेह हैं । हम ने कहा था कि हर घर को बिजली देंगे, हर गांव को बिजली देंगे । आज हर गांव में बिजलीघर देने का प्रयास किया जा रहा है । वर्ष 2022 तक सभी को हमने घर देने का संकल्प लिया है । एक वर्ष में 01 करोड़ 95 लाख मकान मकान बनाने की इच्छाशक्ति भारतीय जनता पार्टी, एनडीए की सरकार में है । खुद वित्त मंत्री जी ने कहा है कि 314 दिनों में एक प्रधान मंत्री आवास बनता था, अब वह मात्र 114 दिनों में बनेगा । आप गांव जाइए । मुंडा जी यहां बैठे हुए हैं । झारखंड के गांवों में जाइए, आदिवासी इलाकों में जाइए, छत्तीसगढ़ में जाइए । …(व्यवधान) मान्यवर, मैंने अभी अपनी बात शुरू की है । मैं सेकेंड वक्ता हूं ।

महोदय, मैं आपके माध्यम से कहना चाहता हूं कि आज हम 01 करोड़ 95 लाख आवास दे रहे हैं । आजादी के बाद, आज हर घर में टॉयलेट्स होने चाहिए थे । हम ने 9 करोड़ टॉयलेट्स बनाए हैं । हम ने ‘उज्ज्वला योजना’ के तहत सात करोड़ चूल्हे बांटे हैं । गांव में कभी कोई क्लीन एनर्जी की कल्पना नहीं कर सकता था ।

आज हम श्रमिकों की बात करते हैं । You are always advocating for the interest of labour and for the protection of labour. I used to endorse even your cause. आज पहली बार आपको महसूस हो रहा होगा कि उन श्रमिकों को प्रति माह तीन हजार रुपये पेंशन देने की बात है । तीन करोड़ खुदरा व्यवसायिओं को वह देने की बात है । एक करोड़ रुपये का लोन 95 मिनट में निकल सकता है । आज फाइव ट्रिलियन अर्थव्यवस्था की बात होती है । देश की आजादी के बाद वर्ष 2014 तक देश की इकोनॉमी क्या थी – 1.85 ट्रिलियन डॉलर । वर्ष 1947 में देश आजाद हुआ और वर्ष 2014 तक देश की अर्थव्यवस्था केवल 1.85 ट्रिलियन डॉलर की थी । वर्ष 2018 में यह 2.7 ट्रिलियन डॉलर थी । हमारा संकल्प है कि हमारा देश तीन ट्रिलियन डॉलर अर्थव्यवस्था वाला देश बने। हम एनडीए की सरकार में ग्यारहवें से छठे स्थान पर आ गये हैं और हम पांचवें स्थान पर पहुंच जाएंगे । आज हम दुनिया में अर्थव्यवस्था के मामले में छठे स्थान पर हैं । …(व्यवधान)

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Please conclude now. There are so many speakers from the BJP.

SHRI JAGDAMBIKA PAL: Sir, I am concluding. मैं ज्यादा समय नहीं लूंगा । आज इलेक्ट्रिक व्हीकल्स की बात हुई है । 

आज महिलाएं हों या श्रमिक हों, जब जन-धन एकाउंट्स खुल रहे थे तो उसे प्रधान मंत्री जी ने एक अभियान बनाया । लोग कहते थे कि गरीबों का जन-धन खाता खुलेगा, उसमें पैसा कहां से आएगा? यह खाता किस लिए खुल रहा है? लोग सरकास्ट‍िक रिमार्क्स पास किया करते थे । आज 33-34 करोड़ प्रधान मंत्री जन-धन खाते खुले । आज उसी जन-धन खाते में वीमेन सेल्फ हेल्प ग्रुप में जीरो बैलेंस पर खाता खुल रहा है । गांव की गरीब महिलाओं को अपने किसी बच्चे या बीमार सदस्य के 105 डिग्री के बुखार की हालत में पांच हजार रुपये की ओवरड्राफ्ट की सुविधा मिल रही है । वे शहर लेकर जाकर उसका इलाज करा सकते हैं । सेल्फ हेल्प ग्रुप से उनको एक लाख रुपये का लोन मिल सकता है ।

आज हम रेलवे में 50 लाख करोड़ रुपये का निवेश करने जा रहे हैं । अगर इन्वेस्टमेंट नहीं होगा तो एम्प्लॉयमेंट नहीं बढ़ेगा और एम्प्लॉयमेंट नहीं होगा तो जीडीपी नहीं ।

निश्चित तौर से ये सारे विषय आपस में जुड़े हुए हैं । क्या इसी सदन में वर्ष 2014 तक पॉलिसी पैरालिसेस की बात नहीं होती थी? आज पॉलिसी पैरालिसेस की बात नहीं हो रही है । आज ईज़ ऑफ डूइंग बिजनेस की बात हो रही है । आज ईज़ ऑफ लिविंग की बात हो रही है । मैं समझता हूं कि आज देश बदल रहा है । पहले दुनिया में लोग अपने देश से पूंजी निकाल कर यूरोप, अमरीका, साउथ अफ्रीका में इन्वेस्ट कर रहे थे, लेकिन आज स्थिति बदल गई है । आज चाहे दावोस का आर्थिक सम्मेलन हो, चाहे ब्रिक्स का सम्मेलन हो, चाहे जी-20 का सम्मेलन हो, आसियान का सम्मेलन हो, यूनाइटेड नेशन्स का सम्मेलन हो, अब दुनिया में जब हमारे प्रधान मंत्री जाते हैं, तो वर्ल्ड के लीडर बनकर इमर्ज करते हैं और पूरी दुनिया हमारी तरफ देख रही है कि ईज़ ऑफ डूइंग बिजनेस के लिए हमारा देश एक अच्छा मुल्क है ।

माननीय सभापति : आप अपनी बात समाप्त कीजिए ।

श्री जगदम्बिका पाल : मान्यवर, मैं कहना चाहता हूं कि डायरेक्ट टैक्सेस बढ़े हैं । पैन कार्ड हो या न हो, आधार कार्ड मान्य कर दिया । मुकेश जी बैठे हैं, जिस गांव में भी जाएं, किसी भी पार्टी का एमपी हो, हर एमपी से सबसे पहले गांव का व्यक्ति मांग करता है कि हमारे गांव को भी प्रधान मंत्री ग्राम सड़क योजना से जोड़ दीजिए । आज देश का हर गांव इस योजना से जुड़े, उसके लिए 1,25,000 किलोमीटर सड़क बनाने का प्रावधान इस बजट में किया गया है । पहले हम लोग थोड़ी-थोड़ी सड़क के लिए प्रस्ताव भेजते थे । मैं समझता हूं कि हर संसदीय क्षेत्र के सांसदों के गांव की कनेक्टिविटी इस योजना के माध्यम से होगी, जिसके लिए 80,250 करोड़ रुपये का प्रावधान किया गया है ।

माननीय सभापति : आप कृपया बैठ जाएं । आपकी पार्टी के भी 30 से ज्यादा सदस्यों ने अपनी बात कहनी है ।

श्री जगदम्बिका पाल: मैं सिर्फ इतना मेंशन करना चाहता हूं कि कितना एलोकेशन पीएमजीएसवाई योजना के लिए किया गया है । अभी तक घरों में शौचालय नहीं था, बिजली कनेक्शन नहीं था, आवास नहीं था, गैस नहीं थी । हमने साढ़े पांच लाख से ऊपर गांवों को ओडीएफ किया है, 9 करोड़ शौचालय बनाए हैं । 256 जिलों के 1592 ब्लॉक डार्क जोन हो रहे थे । वहां पानी की कमी थी । लोग कहते हैं कि थर्ड वर्ल्ड वॉर पानी पर होगा । अधीर रंजन जी भी कह रहे थे । हम भी उस डिबेट में भाग ले रहे थे । निश्चित तौर पर मैं कह रहा हूं कि यह संकल्प हो कि हर गांव में हम बिजली पहुंचा सकते हैं, हर घर को उज्ज्वला दे सकते हैं, हर घर को शौचालय दे सकते हैं, ऐसे ही हमारी सरकार हर घर को जल देगी । इस बजट का ध्येय ‘जल और जीवन’ है । ‘हर घर को जल और हर घर के नौजवान का बेहतर कल, यही हमारा है संकल्प ।’

SHRI PRADYUT BORDOLOI (NOWGONG): Hon. Chairperson Sir, thank you for giving me this opportunity to participate in the General Discussion on the General Budget, 2019. 

One was really elated to listen to the Budget speech of the hon. Finance Minister on the 5th of July, 2019. It was a fine seamless blending of English, Hindi, Urdu and Tamil. She gave us a lot of hope but during her speech when she started to elaborate on the real issues, the hon. Finance Minister urged the hon. Members to refer to the annexure to the Budget speech to know about the specifics. 

When one goes through the specifics, the Budget speech turned out to be a façade an empty rhetoric and non-philosophy. The hon. Finance Minister, in her Budget speech, promised the country a journey towards a five trillion-dollar economy, a journey with the slowest pace in the last 15 years! In the last five years, the economy of India, no matter what the Government claims as India is the second fastest growing economy was actually lumbering painfully. With prudent policy management India should have surpassed China. But with the slowest pace in economic growth, are we supposed to reach that five trillion-dollar economy within the targeted period?

The Economic Survey says that India has envisaged a growth rate of eight per cent but eight per cent growth is nowhere to be seen in round the corner. If we were to reach the target of five trillion dollars economy, we have to grow at the rate of 12 per cent and not eight per cent. The gap between receipts and expenditure in our budget is nearly 25 per cent. The Budget speech indicates that this gap has to be bridged by borrowings. The borrowings of Rs. 7 lakh crore is not a small figure. The hon. Finance Minister also has indicated that the country might resort to the external borrowings for bridging the gap. Not being sceptical, it reminds us of cases of Latin American countries like Venezuela, Chile or some other countries having resorted to the reckless external borrowings. So, when it comes to External Borrowings we would like to know the action plan of the Government of India, if it resorts to external borrowings, like at what rate, what would be the return and what would be the repayment period. This country has the right to know about the action plan of any such external borrowings.

A Budget is not merely an account of receipts and expenditure or an account of fiscal deficit or financial concessions. A Budget is actually a philosophy. A Budget should actually be a roadmap for tangible implementation of that philosophy. So, this Budget should give us the roadmap. 

And the primary aim of any Budget of the Government of India should be to generate income and employment. It is a matter of grave concern that we are facing an unprecedented job crisis in India today. I would just quote the figures in this regard. In 2011-12, unemployment rate was 3.8 per cent which jumped to five per cent in 2015-16. As per the latest report of the National Sample Survey Office which was released last June, unemployment rate has jumped to 6.2 per cent in 2017-18. Sir, it is not a joke. The slow and steady rise of the figure has been attributed to subdued investment and stunted growth of our manufacturing sector. Even today, this Government has failed to give us a National Manufacturing Policy. This Government has failed to give us an Industrial Policy that would boost or accelerate the growth of the manufacturing sector and multiply economic activities. The Periodical Labour Force Study Report released by the National Sample Survey Office in June, 2019 clearly states that unemployment rose by 3.5 per cent over the figures of 2012-13.

What is alarming is that only in the year 2017-18, thirty millions or three crores of our working force got failed. Three crore people in 2017-18 alone lost their jobs and became unemployed. This figure is really a matter of big concern. 

Now, what are the tools of job creation provided by this Budget? This is the question now. Like unemployment problem, there is another big crisis looming over us and that is the agrarian crisis. We all know that 55 per cent of our working population, basically, is engaged in the agricultural sector. But what is the contribution of the agricultural sector to our GDP? It is merely 17 per cent. Why does this mean? This means that we have huge disguised unemployment in the agricultural sector. There is a lot of scope to increase and to accelerate the growth of agrarian economy. 

The Prime Minister’s Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana is a nice policy, but it is only a subsidy. It is not an investment in the agrarian sector. I come from Assam. About 75 per cent of our farmers in Assam are still settled with a single crop. Assam, probably, has the most fertile land. But if we invest in watershed management, if we invest in irrigation, if we invest in mechanisation, and if we go for multi-cropping, the agrarian income and the rural income will multiply. These are the areas where investment is required and budget remains mum. 

The Finance Minister has actually given us a lot of hope that the job crisis will decrease and the agrarian economy will accelerate because of private sector investment. But where is the private sector investment? There are no signs of optimism in the private sector and .…(Interruptions) Fresh private sector investment plunged to a 15-year low figure. Even public sector’s new projects failed by a staggering 41 per cent in the last five years.

The public sector projects are being stalled at an all-time figure of 26 per cent. Make in India has been a monumental failure. What would be the boosting formula? The Budget has not provided anything.…(Interruptions)

SHRI PRADYUT BORDOLOI : I would like to tell you one thing. I come from the North-Eastern Region.…(Interruptions) I just want to say that the great Indian nation strives on pluralism. …(Interruptions) The great Indian nation is not consolidated by a singular idea or Hindutva. Otherwise, the centripetal tendency of the core will degenerate into centrifugal tendency.…(Interruptions)

SHRI PRADYUT BORDOLOI : There will be a tendency of secession if you do not reach out to the periphery. You cannot impose a unitary or singular idea on the idea of pluralism.

श्री वैद्यनाथ प्रसाद महतो (वाल्मीकि नगर): माननीय सभापति महोदय, सर्वप्रथम आम बजट पर बोलने का जो आपने अवसर दिया है, इसके लिए हृदय से धन्यवाद देता हूं । देश की पूर्णकालिक पहली महिला वित्त मंत्री श्रीमती निर्मला सीतारमण जी ने जो बजट पेश किया है, उसके लिए वे बधाई की पात्र हैं । उनको मैं विशेष रूप से धन्यवाद देता हूं कि उन्होंने जनप्रिय मुख्य मंत्री माननीय श्री नीतीश कुमार जी के ‘’सात निश्चय’’ योजना में से एक योजना ‘हर घर नल, हर घर जल’ को अपनाने की बात कही है। भारत गांवों का देश है । भारत की आत्मा गांवों में बसती है । गांव, गरीब और किसान के बारे में आम बजट में जिक्र किया गया है । 

आम बजट में किसानों के लिए, गरीबों के लिए सराहनीय कदम उठाया गया है, उसके लिए सदन के माध्यम से माननीय प्रधान मंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र भाई मोदी जी को तहे दिल से धन्यवाद देता हूं । महोदय, जहां से मैं बोल रहा हूं, वह न्याय का सबसे बड़ा मन्दिर है । न्याय के मन्दिर में राजनीति से ऊपर उठकर देशहित और जनहित की बातें हमें कहनी चाहिए । सत्य को सत्य और असत्य को असत्य कहना चाहिए । चूंकि इस कार्यवाही को न केवल देश की सवा सौ करोड़ जनता किसी न किसी रूप में देख और सुन रही है, बल्कि सम्पूर्ण विश्व की नजर भी इस कार्यवाही पर है । 

महोदय, आजादी के 70 वर्ष बाद भी समाज में कहीं धूप तो कहीं छाया है, कोई हंस रहा है तो कोई रो रहा है, कहीं गरीबी है तो कहीं अमीरी है । इस खाई को पाटने की आवश्यकता है । इंसान-इंसान को रिक्शे पर ढोता है । अभी समाज में ऐसे भी लोग हैं जो पेट के सहारे ठेला चला रहे हैं । उनको कितना कष्ट होता होगा, यह सदन को सोचना चाहिए । अभी भी देश में ऐसे गरीब हैं जो कंबल और रजाई की जगह चड्ढी और बोरा ओढ़ते हैं । कवि ने कहा है कि – ‘गरीबों की आह में भगवान बसते हैं ।’ अत: हम सभी को गरीबों की सेवा करनी चाहिए । जेठ, बैसाख की कड़ाके की धूप में जब किसान कंधे पर हल और कुदाल लेकर खेत में काम करने जाता है, तो उसके माथे से पसीना टपकता हुआ उसके पैरों के तलवे तक आता है । उसी में भगवान का दर्शन होता है । इसलिए गरीबों, मजदूरों, रिक्शा-ठेला चलाने वाले और समाज के दबे-कुचले लोगों को राहत कैसे हो, इस पर हम सभी को सोचना चाहिए । 

महोदय, मैं बिहार की ओर आपका ध्यान ले जाना चाहता हूं । वर्ष 2000 में बिहार और झारखण्ड का बंटवारा हुआ । सभी प्राकृतिक संपदा, धन संपदा, कल-कारखाने झारखण्ड में चले गए और बिहार में सिर्फ बालू और नदियां ही बचीं । कोसी नदी, गंडक नदी, महानंदा नदी और गंगा नदी की बाढ़ से सारा बिहार बाढ़ की चपेट में आ जाता है । इससे निजात दिलाने की जरूरत है । बिहार के लोकप्रिय मुख्य मंत्री श्री नीतीश कुमार जी ने अपने कार्यकाल में बिहार को काफी मजबूत किया है । बिहार वासियों की आशा भरी नजरें बरबस ही आपकी ओर हैं । देश के लोकप्रिय प्रधान मंत्री को बिहार जैसे गरीब राज्य को विशेष राज्य का दर्जा देना चाहिए । यदि वे यह दर्जा देते हैं तो उनकी बड़ी कृपा होगी । 

महोदय, मैं जहां से दूसरी बार सांसद चुनकर आया हूं वह संसदीय क्षेत्र वाल्मीकि नगर के नाम से जाना जाता है । यह क्षेत्र महर्षि वाल्मीकि की तपोभूमि, लव-कुश की जन्मभूमि, चाणक्य की कर्मभूमि है । वाल्मीकि नगर हिमालय की गोद में अवस्थित दर्जनों नदियों से युक्त मनोरम स्थल है । यह महात्मा गांधी की कर्मभूमि के नाम से भी विख्यात है । यहां चार लाख लोग थारू आदिवासी जनजाति समाज के हैं, जो काफी मेहनती होते हुए भी गरीब हैं । इस क्षेत्र के विकास के लिए माननीय मुख्य मंत्री श्री नीतीश कुमार जी ने समेकित थरुहट विकास अभिकरण बनाकर इस क्षेत्र का काफी विकास किया है, फिर भी यह क्षेत्र पिछड़ा है । 

महोदय, यह क्षेत्र दर्जनों पहाड़ और नदियों से घिरा हुआ है । अनेक नदियों पर बड़े-बड़े पुल बनाने की आवश्यकता है । यहां जनजाति के लोग रहते हैं, जिनको एक प्रतिशत का आरक्षण मिला है । वहां के जनजाति के लोग आरक्षण बढ़ाने की मांग करते हैं । सरकार को इस पर भी विचार करना चाहिए । थारू वनवासी लोग खेलकूद, संगीत और नाच-गाने में बहुत अधिक अभिरुचि रखते हैं । इसके लिए क्षेत्र में स्टेडियम बनाने की जरूरत है । हमारे क्षेत्र में अभी भी केन्द्रीय विद्यालय नहीं है । केन्द्रीय विद्यालय की स्थापना होनी चाहिए ।

माननीय सभापति: प्लीज समाप्त कीजिए ।

श्री वैद्यनाथ प्रसाद महतो : महोदय, क्षेत्रवासियों की मांग है कि केन्द्रीय विद्यालय की स्थापना यथाशीघ्र करवाई जाए । संचार के लिए इस क्षेत्र में अभी तक टावर नहीं लगा है । यहां टावर लगाने की व्यवस्था अतिशीघ्र की जानी चाहिए । नरकटियागंज में रक्सौल, गोरखपुर और सीतामढ़ी से ट्रेनें आती हैं, लेकिन वहां से कोच की धुलाई और सफाई का काम नहीं हो पाता है । अत: इसकी भी व्यवस्था की जानी चाहिए । बगहा रेलवे स्टेशन पर वीआईपी रूम की आवश्यकता है ।

माननीय सभापति: प्लीज कनक्लूड कीजिए ।

श्री वैद्यनाथ प्रसाद महतो : महोदय, नरकटियागंज स्टेशन पर फूड प्लाजा की व्यवस्था होनी चाहिए । इस क्षेत्र में गोरखपुर, उत्तर प्रदेश से होते हुए बगहा, नरकटियागंज, बेतिया, मुजफ्फरपुर होते हुए …(व्यवधान)

माननीय सभापति: रेलवे मिनिस्ट्री का अगला डिसक्शन है, उसमें आप बोल सकते हैं ।

श्री वैद्यनाथ प्रसाद महतो: पटना तक पूर्ण रूप से ट्रेनें चलती थीं, आज ट्रेनें बंद हैं । जैसे ट्रेन संख्या 55042 डाउन गाड़ी पैसेंजर और गाड़ी संख्या 55041 पाटलीपुत्र से संध्या 6 बजे चलकर बगहा सुबह 4.30 बजे पहुंचती थी, वह बंद है । उसको चालू करने की जरूरत है । ट्रेन संख्या 55030 गोरखपुर से चलकर बगहा, नरकटियागंज, बेतिया होते हुए मुजफ्फरपुर सुबह पहुंचती थी ।

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Hon. Member, you can speak on this point during the Railway Budget. We are going to discuss it separately. Now, please conclude. 

श्री वैद्यनाथ प्रसाद महतो : हम मांग करते हैं कि उसकी आवश्यकता है ।

महोदय, अंत में उपर्युक्त सभी मांगों को ध्यान में रखते हुए, सहानुभूतिपूर्वक विचार करना चाहिए । साथ ही एक बात कहना चाहते हैं कि चम्पारण जिला गन्ना उत्पादक है । वहां की चीनी मिलें गन्ने का दाम नहीं दे रही हैं । किसानों में आक्रोश है ।

SHRIMATI APARAJITA SARANGI (BHUBANESWAR): Hon. Chairman, Sir, I consider it to be my privilege to be able to speak in this august House on our Government’s Budget, which was presented to this House by Madam Nirmala Sitharamanji on 5th July, 2019. This particular Budget is the reflection of the extraordinary balance between intent and content, vision and provision. 

I am reminded of a line from Victor Hugo, a French poet, who had said: ‘No power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come.” Now, I would definitely like to put in here that the time of crystallisation of hon. Prime Minister’s idea of ‘New India’ has come. This particular Budget provides the building blocks for ‘New India’.

If you read the Budget, five words actually stand out. They are very powerful words. One is ‘aspirational’; Number two is ‘structural’; Number three is ‘transformational’; Number 4 is ‘inclusive’; and Number 5 is ‘sustainable’.

It is a highly aspirational Budget. We are talking of a $ 5 trillion economy, which would be achieved by 2024. But at the same time, this particular aspiration is an affirmation of Prime Minister’s slogan: ‘Reform, Perform and Transform’; and this is something, which Prime Minister is not leaving for the successive Governments to realise. He is basically calling upon the collective will of the people of India, collective strength of the people of India and collective energy of the people of India to transform our country into a middle level economy.

So, from here, I would like to list out some of the points. There is paucity of time, I understand. But I would definitely like to place before this House some of the issues that actually are brought out very well in this particular Budget of ours.

Sir, there is a discourse; there is a declaration of Rs. 100 lakh crore for infrastructure development by 2024. The Budget Speech also talks of formation of an expert committee which will look into the ways and means of resource mobilisation which is definitely a very good step in the right direction. 

Thirdly, I was quite amused in the morning when hon. Member, Mr. Shashi Tharoor, talked of suit-boot-ki-sarkar. This particular Budget is focussed on dwelling upon gaon, garib aur kisan. The other day, during the weekend, I have been to one of the villages in my Constituency. Many villagers were there. One of the villagers stood up and said: “We are getting five things from the Government: First is the toilet, second is the cooking gas facility, third is roof over our head, fourth is electricity and fifth is the piped water supply by 2024. What more do we need?”, and he said: “Please go to Delhi and convey our gratitude to hon. Prime Minister.” This is the message from the villagers of my Constituency, Bhubaneshwar in Odisha. 

We are talking of a new Education Policy. We are talking of the Higher Education Commission. This, particular, Commission is very much required. In fact, if we are talking of getting all the students from foreign countries, as many students as possible come to India and study, this is a very welcome move and a welcome initiative of the Government of India. I would like to place before the House that by rough estimates, eight billion to ten billion dollars are spent by Indian students who are studying outside. If we are able to have institutes of academic excellence here, our children will not go outside and children from outside will come here. So, we will be earning foreign exchange on the one hand and saving our foreign exchange on the other.

The Budget also talks of the National Research Foundation. The National Research Foundation is a right step in the right direction. We have to fund; we have to coordinate; and we have to promote research and development in the country. I would like to point out here that this is a very timely intervention of the Government and we must commend the efforts of the Government and the hon. Finance Minister for this because India is spending 0.88 per cent of the expenditure whereas Sweden is spending 4.1 per cent of the expenditure. USA is spending 2.8 per cent of the expenditure and, I think, it is China is spending 2.1 per cent of the expenditure. So, it is the right time to think about promotion of research and development in the country. We need to align with emerging areas of bio-technology, bio-engineering, robotics, and artificial intelligence which this, particular Government, our Government, is planning to do in the days to come. 

I would like to talk about the self-help groups. I would like to talk about the PMGSY. I would also like to talk about Green Budgeting. We never ever heard of Green Budgeting. In fact, my predecessor, the earlier speaker from my Party, had already said about SHGs. It is a wonderful thing. We are going one step ahead of the National Rural Livelihood Mission. We are talking of Rs. 5,000 overdraft. We are talking of Rs. 1 lakh to one particular SHG member under the MUDRA Scheme. We are talking of interest subvention for all the districts of the country. This is a very welcome step. 

I would also like to mention about the PMGSY. The other day, the hon. Finance Minister mentioned on the Floor of the House that as far as PMGSY is concerned, we have started constructing 130 kilometres to 135 kilometres of roads per day. Keeping in view the fact that this is a wonderful intervention of the Government connecting all the roads, all the farm networks, connecting our farmers to the markets, this particular Government, our Government, has, actually, earmarked Rs. 80,250 crore. It will be constructing 1,25,000 kilometre of roads in the days to come. 

I would also like to mention here about Green Budgeting. We are talking of solid waste management. We are also talking of the usage of plastic waste in the PMGSY roads. 

These are very welcome initiatives. We are talking of reducing of GST and bringing GST down from 12 per cent to five per cent so that consumers can afford electric vehicles. These are very welcome steps, path-breaking initiatives and hon. Prime Minister and the entire team needs to be commended for this initiative.

Let me honestly tell you, I was hearing all my friends since morning. We were all sitting and we were all listening to them. Let us all work together in such a manner that we unitedly disprove that cynicism is the national disease of India. We should not be cynics; we should not be pessimist. In fact, I am reminded of Helen Keller. The other day I was going through one of her books. She said: “No pessimist ever discovered the secret of the stars, or sailed to an uncharted land, or opened a new heaven for the human spirit”. Let us not be pessimist. Let us be optimist; let us rise to commend and let us say that this is a wonderful Budget. 

The recapitalisation of banks by pumping in Rs. 70,000 crore is a wonderful initiative. I must say this because we are ensuring credit flow and we are also ensuring that there are greater levels of private investment. This is something which we really need to commend the Government about. 

If you look at the Budget, there is the highest-ever allocation to agriculture sector. How do we call it ‘suit-boot ki Sarkar’? How do we call it the Sarkar of big businessmen? We are talking of garib; we are talking of kisan; we are talking of gaon; we are talking of vendors in the urban areas; we are talking of youth; we are talking of women. All the vulnerable sections of society are being taken care of. I would like to mention here that this is a huge budget and there is the highest-ever allocation to agriculture sector which includes Rs. 87,000 crore under the PM-KISAN scheme which is a very welcome step. We are talking of reforms through e-NAM. We are talking of reforms through APMCs. We are talking of 10,000 farmer-producer organisations. These are wonderful steps. 

This particular Budget is different from other Budgets of pre-2014 Governments. There are two things which I would like to mention here. We are not talking of vast schemes and grandiose theories. Vast schemes and grandiose theories will not achieve the same benefits as the accumulation of smaller, consistent and attainable goals. This particular Budget indicates that our country should be an example of what the sum would look like when all the smaller parts that actually work are added up. 

I am really very thankful to the entire team of hon. Finance Minister. Under the direction of hon. Prime Minister, a wonderful document has been prepared. This particular Budget is a great document. Let me honestly tell you, this particular Budget is not a collection of numbers. In the morning, some of my friends were saying, “Where are the numbers? Earlier there were numbers; there are no numbers.” It is not a question of giving numbers. It is an expression of the values and aspirations of our Government, of our people. So, this Budget is of a very high quality and we should commend the Government for it.

I have worked in the Rural Development Department for five years; I had the privilege of handling MGNREGA. We were talking of water conservation; we were talking of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY). We were talking of ‘per drop, more crop’ idea of hon. Prime Minister. We have graduated to the next level now. We are consolidating all the Departments working in ivory towers of isolation and we are talking of a Jal Shakti Mantralaya which is a wonderful initiative.

If there is a third world war, it is said, it will be around water. We are aware of the depleting water levels. We are aware of the erratic monsoon. There are many questions in the Lok Sabha in the last couple of days, I am seeing, on the issue of less water in the reservoirs. So, we are going to face a terrible water crisis. Just think of the foresightedness of this Government, our Government. I am so proud that I am a part of this Government. 

I am proud to be part of the hon. Prime Minister’s team. This particular Government has understood the need for working towards water conservation and water management, and that is why, we have the Jal Shakti Ministry. That is why, all provisioning has been given for ensuring piped water supply to every household by 2024. It reflects the courage of conviction. Otherwise, it is very difficult. We are talking of seven lakh villages. We are talking of 69 per cent of the population of our country. What courage of the Government to say that these five things—I counted them—will be given to each household! I will repeat them. We are talking of toilets; we are talking of cooking gas; we are talking of electricity; we are talking of a roof over head; and we are talking of piped water supply. What more do we require? It requires courage of conviction which has been shown by the Government in vast measure. This particular Budget needs all appreciation.

SHRI TOKHEHO YEPTHOMI: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I rise to participate in the General Discussion on the Budget presented to this august House on 5th of July, 2019.

Hon. Chairman, Sir, the Budget presented by the hon. Finance Minister is a very calculative and a balanced Budget. As I look at the Budget speech given by the hon. Finance Minister, it is first of its kind that has been presented in this august House.

In the last five years, the hon. Prime Minister has been talking about cashless transaction in the country. I have also been thinking how this cashless transaction will be successful in the coming days. But the vision of the hon. Prime Minister is going a long way. The hon. Finance Minister has proposed to impose two per cent tax on those people who withdraw more than Rs.1 crore at a time. 

This is a strong step that has been taken by the hon. Finance Minister. By implementing it, first, the Government will be able to control the circulation of counterfeit money in the country; secondly, this will improve tax collection and thirdly, this will encourage people to avoid cash transactions. I also commend the proposal of the Government to impose two per cent tax on cash withdrawal of more than Rs.1 crore from a bank account in one financial year. It will encourage people to have easy transactions and avoid cash payments. 

The hon. Finance Minister has presented a Budget with a focus on India’s 10-point ‘Vision for the Decade’ to take this country to a new height. 

The hon. Member who spoke earlier has raised an important issue that the hon. Finance Minister has focussed on agriculture sector. The Government in its Budget has proposed to give more importance to strengthen agriculture, develop infrastructure, and support private entrepreneurs. Therefore, the Government has increased the budget allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare by over 78 per cent to Rs.1.39 lakh crore. This has been proposed in order to help the farmers and also to uplift the poor and down-trodden people in our country. Thus, more attention has been given to agriculture sector. 

I would also like to raise an important issue on the natural rubber farming in our country, especially in the southern State of Kerala and some North-Eastern States. For the last five or six years, a little over 13,000 lakh natural rubber farmers and a little over five lakh workers have been severely affected because of huge natural rubber import from other countries. If this trend continues, these farmers and workers will remain badly affected. 

According to a report, the import of natural rubber in 2008-09 was 77,762 lakh tonnes which has increased manifold and reached 5,82,351 tonnes in 2018-19. Thus, the increased import of natural rubber over last 10 years has affected these farmers and workers severely. 

The import of natural rubber from other countries will have to be reduced. Unless that is done, there will be no improvement in the conditions of natural rubber farmers and workers in India. Unless the import is reduced, India will remain fully dependent on foreign countries for its strategic raw material. Therefore, I would humbly request the hon. Finance Minister to look into it and reduce the import of natural rubber from other countries. 

Sir, in the last speech of hon. President addressed to Members of both Houses of Parliament on 20th June, 2019, he made a special mention about the development of infrastructure in the North-East, to encourage the farmers in the North-Eastern States and to encourage tourism in the North-Eastern States. When I look at the fund allocation under Demand No. 22 for the Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region, I find that it is only Rs. 3,000 crore. Even the year before, in 2017-18, it was Rs. 3,000 crore. In 2018-19, it was only Rs. 2,865 crore. This year also, it is only Rs. 3,000 crore. 

As I look at the outcome of the Budget 2019-20, the split of this amount of Rs. 3,000 crore is as follows: the North-Eastern Council gets Rs. 885.18 crore; Central pool of resources gets Rs. 666.17 crore; and North-East Special Infrastructure Development Scheme gets Rs. 694.65 crore. When the hon. President of India and the hon. Prime Minister of India have given so much importance to infrastructure development in the North-Eastern States, if the fund allocation remains stagnant at this amount for the North-Eastern States, it will take a long time for them to come up and develop their region. 

If this small Budget allocation goes by the size of the States, naturally, Assam, being the biggest State among the eight North-Eastern States, will get a chunk of funds out of this allocation for the North-Eastern States. I had shared this in my previous speech also. Among eight North-Eastern States, only the State of Assam has railways and airlines, but they do not have waterways while rest of the seven North-Eastern States depend on road transport. Unless road transport is improved in the North-Eastern States, we cannot come at par with rest of the States in the country. Therefore, I want to make a humble request and suggestion to the hon. Finance Minister and hon. Prime Minister to kindly revise the Budget allocation for the development of the North-Eastern States in the coming days.

With these few words, Sir, I thank you for giving me time to participate in the debate on Budget. Thank you.
